messages:
nina: Odd spike on p95 decode for low-latency http2 streams after yesterday's runtime deploy. Affected: streaming-chat endpoints with tiny chunks (~16-48 bytes). p95 up ~30% and we see extra syscall traps on the host.
cheng: Which host image / canary? Any flamegraphs or pprof?
nina: canary-stream-7. Short traces: https://perf.redwood/trace/5865001111 and pprof diff attached. Top of stack is tokenizer + http2 frame parse.
alex: Could this be the tokenization pool contention we instrumented last sprint? We changed tokenizer worker count to be proportional to concurrency (PR #510). If lots of tiny frames come in, workers might be thrashing.
jiro: Also saw increased HPACK decompress time on small headers in grpc/http2 path earlier this week (gateway PR #522 adjusted header reuse). HPACK costs blow up with many small frames due to per-frame header blocks.
nina: Perf excerpt (sampling):
```
# simplified hotspots
tokenizer_worker_read+0x120 22%
http2_decode_frame+0x81       17%
hpack_decompress+0x4c        13%
kernel_selector_score+0x2e    9%
kv_cache_lookup+0x50          6%
```
cheng: kernel_selector_score is interesting. Any selector rule changes? We merged a dynamic-batch-first heuristic last week (PR #517) that prefers throughput kernels when expected batch >1. For tiny streaming frames expected batch is 1 but estimator was overpredicting because it uses a 200ms window.
ajiro: typo: I'm jiro, not ajiro :) but yea estimator smoothing causes misprediction and picks a heavier kernel with larger L3 footprint. That hurts small-frame latency because host prep + cache line churn increases.
Alex: Quick experiments? We can: (A) pin tokenizer workers to a fixed small pool, (B) tighten estimator smoothing window, (C) tweak gRPC/h2 coalescing to merge tiny writes so fewer frames.
nina: I ran A+B in sandbox. Results: p95 dropped ~18% when pinning workers to 4 and reducing estimator alpha (less smoothing). However p50 barely moved. C (proxy coalesce) reduced syscall rate but increased tokenization batch size slightly and gave mixed latency results.
cheng: Sounds like multi-root cause. Proposal: 1) revert estimator smoothing change in canary-stream-7 (fastfix), 2) add a runtime override to pick lightweight kernel for streams marked low-frame-size, 3) add a session-level KV pin for streaming sessions to avoid repeated kv_cache lookups on re-warm.
ijiro: I'll own (2). Implement a "stream_hint" path where ingress marks requests with avg_frame_size < 64 and the selector weights host-overhead lower. Patch branch: runtime/stream-kernel-hint.
nina: I'll test (1) and (3) on canary and run a 6-hour window. I'll also gather syscall traces (strace-ish) to show writev/readv counts.
alex: For (3) consider ephemeral pin with LRU and TTL tuned to session duration (30-120s). We don't want permanent pins hurting memory. Also add metrics: kv.pin.hits and kv.pin.evictions.
perf-bot: [automated] created perf-issue #2077 and attached traces + pprof diffs.
cheng: If canary metrics look good, we do a fastfix rollback of estimator and push the stream_hint patch behind a feature flag for 2 weeks before broad rollout. Also follow up: re-evaluate tokenizer worker autoscaling heuristic.
jiro: I'll open PR and a short benchmark harness that simulates many concurrent tiny streams to validate.
nina: Thanks everyone. Will update with telemetry in ~3h. :raised_hands:
